title: Hysteresis in Atomic Josephson Junctions
authors: Vijay Pal Singh, Ludwig Mathey, Luigi Amico
abstract: Hysteresis and retrapping are hallmarks of underdamped Josephson dynamics, yet they have remained elusive in atomic Josephson junctions. Here, we introduce a velocity-sweep protocol to demonstrate these phenomena in the underdamped regime of an atomic Josephson junction. Specifically, using classical-field simulations of a two-dimensional bosonic superfluid, we show hysteresis in the velocity-imbalance characteristics and determine the retrapping current. The dynamics are quantitatively captured by the resistively and capacitively shunted junction (RCSJ) model. We show that hysteresis originates from persistent phase slips below the critical current, with the associated dissipation mediated by vortex-antivortex pair nucleation at the weak link. The retrapping current follows the Stewart-McCumber scaling of underdamped junctions, establishing a common phase-dynamical framework for atomic and superconducting Josephson junctions.
summary: This research demonstrates the existence of hysteresis and retrapping in atomic Josephson junctions using bosonic superfluids. By simulating a velocity-sweep protocol, the authors show that these phenomena are governed by phase-slip dynamics, establishing a quantitative link between atomic and superconducting Josephson junction physics. This confirms that AJJs serve as a robust platform for studying fundamental non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of demonstrating and understanding hysteresis and retrapping phenomena in atomic Josephson junctions (AJJs), which are key signatures of underdamped Josephson dynamics.
main_result: Hysteresis and retrapping are successfully demonstrated in AJJs, confirming that the dynamics are governed by persistent phase-slip mechanisms analogous to superconducting junctions.
method: The study employs classical-field simulations using a velocity-sweep protocol applied to a two-dimensional bosonic superfluid model.
model_or_system: The system is an Atomic Josephson Junction (AJJ) modeled using a semiclassical-field approach within the truncated Wigner approximation. The dynamics are compared against the Resistively and Capacitively Shunted Junction (RCSJ) model.
key_observables: Hysteresis width, retrapping current, particle imbalance ($\Delta z$), and the junction response ($\Delta z$ vs. velocity $v$).
important_parameters: Stewart–McCumber parameter ($ eta_C$), critical current ($I_c$), and sweep time ($T_s$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on classical-field simulations and assumes the system can be mapped onto the RCSJ framework for comparison.
figures_summary: Figures show time evolution of density difference, $\Delta z$ vs. barrier velocity $v$ curves demonstrating hysteresis, and the dependence of hysteresis width on sweep time.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the AJJ system and the need to study hysteresis. It details the velocity-sweep protocol and simulation setup, presents the results showing hysteresis matching RCSJ predictions, and concludes by establishing a common phase-dynamical framework.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges the physics of superconducting Josephson junctions with ultracold atomic systems, providing a clean, controllable platform (bosonic superfluids) to study fundamental non-equilibrium quantum dynamics like phase slips and hysteresis.

Solid lines are power-law fits to the late-time behavior, hw(Ts) ∼T −η s . (c) Ir/Ic as a function of βC.
